grading_method: Evaluator manually compared every requested material part of each answer with the fixed source-backed key and frozen summary; support labels did not determine grades. Key details not requested by question are not mandatory.

grades.question: How are Factory cards, encounter tokens, and the structure bonus set up, and who starts?
grades.expected_answer: Shuffle Factory cards; select players+1 face-down and return others unseen to box. Put an encounter token on each of 11 marked territories. Randomly select one face-up structure bonus tile. Lowest numbered Player Mat starts, then clockwise.
grades.observed_answer: Select number of players + 1 Factory cards at random, place them face-down on the board, and return the rest to the box without looking. Put one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories. Randomly choose a structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts; play proceeds clockwise.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup: ‘randomly select number of players + 1’; ‘11 marked territories’; ‘Randomly choose one structure bonus tile’; ‘The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.’
grades.reason: Factory selection/count/unseen return, 11 encounters, random face-up tile and lowest-mat starter resolved.

grades.question: What starts on the map and each mat, and which mat supplies starting power, combat cards, popularity, coins and objectives?
grades.expected_answer: Character on own home base; one worker on each of two land-adjoined territories. Faction Mat supplies power/combat cards, holds four mechs and six stars. Player Mat supplies popularity/coins/objectives, holds six technology cubes on black-square green boxes, four structures, four recruits and remaining six workers on Produce; action token starts beside it.
grades.observed_answer: At setup, each character starts at its home base; two workers start, one on each of the two land-adjoined territories adjoining the home base. Four mechs begin over the four Faction Mat abilities, six stars by the faction emblem, six technology cubes in black-square green boxes, four structures in matching Player Mat boxes, four recruits in bottom-row circles, six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles, and the action token beside the Player Mat ready for placement. Starting power and combat-card draw come from the Faction Mat; starting popularity, coins, and two objective cards come from the Player Mat.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup steps 3–4: ‘Use the Faction Mat to set starting power and combat-card draw’; ‘Use the Player Mat to set starting popularity, coins and objectives’; starting-piece table/list.
grades.reason: Map and mat pieces, action-token starting location and correct assignment of starting values resolved.

grades.question: May you skip both actions, repeat a section, use top-row gains below, or take the bottom action first? How are costs and benefits determined?
grades.expected_answer: Must move token to different section, except Rusviet may repeat including Factory. Top then bottom, each optional once; may skip both. May use top gains below. Pay full exposed red-box cost before taking as much or as little exposed green benefit as desired.
grades.observed_answer: You must move the token to a different section each turn, but may take neither action (a legal dead turn), either action, or both. If taking both, take top before bottom; you cannot return to top afterward. Rusviet may repeat a section, including its Factory card. Top-row gains may pay bottom-row costs. Pay all exposed red-box costs in full before the action, then choose as much or as little of exposed green-box benefits as desired. Exact costs and coin benefits vary by Player Mat and upgrades; use your mat. You cannot pay only part of a cost.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: ‘different section’; ‘bottom first is not allowed’; ‘Rusviet may repeat’; ‘first pay the full cost’; ‘benefits need not all be taken.’
grades.reason: Mandatory token move, optional actions/ordering, Rusviet exception, top gains below, exposed full costs/optional gains resolved.

grades.question: Who controls a structure territory occupied by an enemy worker, who can use the structure, and from where may you spend resources for an action elsewhere?
grades.expected_answer: Enemy worker controls territory and resources; structure owner retains abilities except cannot Produce at an uncontrolled Mill; enemy gains no structure ability. Spend resources from any controlled territories for actions anywhere; spent resources go to supply.
grades.observed_answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure’s territory controls it and its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure’s abilities; you retain those abilities even without control, except a Mill cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory. Pay action resources from any territories you currently control, even when taking the action elsewhere.
grades.reader_evidence: Control, resources and home bases: ‘An enemy worker alone on your structure’s territory controls it’; ‘Enemy units do not gain your structure’s abilities’; ‘Pay costs using resources from any territories you currently control.’
grades.reason: Enemy worker control, owner-only persistent structure ability/Mill exception and remote resource spending resolved.

grades.question: On a normal unupgraded Move, can one unit move twice, can a transported worker subsequently move, and who can carry what?
grades.expected_answer: Move up to two different units one adjacent territory each, sequentially, or gain $1 instead. All units carry any number of resources; only mechs carry any number of own workers, not characters. Carriage is not the worker movement so worker can subsequently move itself.
grades.observed_answer: No. On normal Move, you may move up to two different units one adjacent territory each; you cannot use both selections to move the same unit twice. All units can pick up, carry, and drop any number of resources. Only mechs may also carry any number of your workers, never your character. A carried worker may subsequently move itself, or it may move onto a mech and be carried by that mech’s later move.
grades.reader_evidence: Move OR coins: ‘two different units, one adjacent territory each’; ‘cannot use both selections to move the same unit twice’; carried workers may subsequently move themselves.
grades.reason: Distinct-unit movement, transported worker own movement and all resource/mech worker transport restrictions resolved.

grades.question: What happens when a Speed-enabled mech enters enemy workers only, even at zero popularity; may its workers enter that territory by themselves?
grades.expected_answer: Mech stops and cannot move again this turn. Enemy workers immediately retreat home leaving resources; attacker loses one popularity each to minimum zero, still retreats them. Workers cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.
grades.observed_answer: A Speed-enabled mech entering a territory occupied only by enemy workers stops and cannot move again that turn. Those workers immediately retreat to their home base, leave resources behind, and you lose one popularity per worker, down to zero; having zero popularity does not prevent the retreat. It is not combat. Your own workers cannot independently move into a territory controlled by enemy workers.
grades.reader_evidence: Move: ‘Your character/mech entering enemy workers only stops’; workers ‘immediately retreat’; ‘Lose one popularity per worker, down to zero’; worker independent-entry restriction.
grades.reason: Enemy-worker-only stop, immediate home retreat/resources, popularity floor and independent worker-entry restriction resolved.

grades.question: When does combat occur after movement, who chooses multiple combat order, and can workers enter or leave enemy-character/mech-controlled territory alone?
grades.expected_answer: Finish all movement, then combats before bottom-row action. Active attacker chooses order. Attacking plastic unit stops on entry and enemy temporarily controls territory. Workers cannot enter or leave such territory independently.
grades.observed_answer: After units finish the Move action, resolve combats before the bottom-row action; complete movement of the other units first. The attacker chooses the order if there are multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of a territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
grades.reader_evidence: Move: finish moving other units, then resolve combats ‘before the bottom-row action’; ‘attacker chooses multiple-combat order’; worker restriction on moving ‘into or out of’ enemy character/mech-controlled territory.
grades.reason: Combat after all movement/before bottom, attacker ordering and independent worker enter/leave prohibition resolved.

grades.question: State Bolster and Trade costs and choices; where are traded resources placed and what if all workers are home? What if the combat deck is exhausted?
grades.expected_answer: Bolster $1 for 2 power OR 1 combat card; Trade $1 for any two resources OR 1 popularity. Place resources on controlled territory with worker; cannot trade for resources with all workers home. Empty combat deck reshuffles discards; if both empty draw none.
grades.observed_answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card, before upgrades; a built Monument also gives one popularity. If the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck; if both deck and discards are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources, same or different, or one popularity, before upgrades; a built Armory also gives one power. Put traded resources on a controlled territory containing at least one worker. If all your workers are at home, you cannot Trade for resources.
grades.reader_evidence: Bolster: ‘Pay $1’; deck exhaustion rule. Trade: ‘any two resources … OR one popularity’; put resources on controlled territory with a worker; cannot Trade resources if all workers are home.
grades.reason: Both $1 top-action choices, worker-controlled trade placement/home prohibition and deck exhaustion branches resolved.

grades.question: How is Produce paid and resolved, where do new workers come from, can benefits be declined, and do new workers change the cost already paid?
grades.expected_answer: Pay all exposed red costs before action, must afford full power/popularity/coins. Choose up to two different controlled territories; each worker may produce one terrain token there. Villages produce workers from Player Mat left to right, after payment, so new exposure affects future Produce costs. May decline production/workers. Workers never return to mat.
grades.observed_answer: Pay every exposed Produce cost (power, popularity, and/or coins) in full before production. Then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades; each worker there may produce one matching terrain token, placed on that territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and are placed in the producing village after payment. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Workers exposed during this Produce affect future Produce costs, not the cost already paid.
grades.reader_evidence: Produce steps 1–3: full cost before production; choose two territories; each worker produces; take new workers from Player Mat left to right after payment; new costs affect future actions.
grades.reason: Full exposed pre-payment, terrain production, left-to-right village workers, optional benefits and future-cost timing resolved.

grades.question: What are Upgrade and Deploy costs, placement restrictions and effects, and can a completed bottom action still be paid?
grades.expected_answer: Upgrade oil: cube from any green box to empty bracketed red box, never solid border. Deploy metal: choose mech on Faction Mat, put on controlled worker territory, never lake; uncovered ability applies to character/all mechs, not workers. Costs/coins vary by mat. Completed bottom action may still be paid for coins and applicable recruit bonus.
grades.observed_answer: Upgrade costs oil: move any technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost; solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded. Deploy costs metal: put any chosen Faction Mat mech on a controlled territory containing your worker, never a lake. Its uncovered ability applies from then on to your character and every mech, not workers. Even after completing all upgrades, mechs, structures, and recruits, you may still pay for that bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
grades.reader_evidence: Bottom-row actions: ‘Upgrade — oil’; ‘Deploy — metal’; placement/effect restrictions; completed actions may still be paid for coins and recruit bonuses.
grades.reason: Oil and metal, placement/effects and completed-action payment are correct. The requested costs are incomplete: the answer never says that the required quantities are the exposed Player Mat amounts, varying by mat/upgrades. Independently adjudicated in expanded01-adjudication.json.

grades.question: Where may a structure be built, can it move or be destroyed, and how do Mill and Mine work when their territories are occupied by enemies?
grades.expected_answer: Build costs wood, controlled worker territory, one structure total per territory; Factory allowed, lakes/home bases forbidden. Permanent cannot move/destroy. Mill adds bonus Produce territory and produces as worker plus actual workers only while controlled. Mine personal tunnel usable for all unit movement even enemy-controlled, enemy cannot use it.
grades.observed_answer: Build costs wood. Place a structure from your Player Mat on a controlled territory with your worker; only one structure total may be on a territory, including opponents’ structures. Factory is allowed; lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. A controlled Mill adds a Produce territory and produces as one worker in addition to actual workers; it cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory. Your Mine is a personal tunnel for your unit movement to and from it even while enemies occupy its territory, subject to ordinary entry/combat restrictions. Opponents cannot use your buildings’ abilities.
grades.reader_evidence: Build — wood; one structure total, Factory allowed, lakes/home bases forbidden; structures cannot move/destroy. Mill control exception and Mine tunnel rule.
grades.reason: Worker/control structure placement, single-structure/terrain restrictions, permanence and enemy-control Mill/Mine exceptions resolved.

grades.question: When enlisting, where does the token go, what are the one-time bonuses, which action sets ongoing bonus, and how do simultaneous/two-player bonuses resolve?
grades.expected_answer: Pay food; remove any recruit from Player Mat, permanently place on open Faction one-time space for 2 power/coins/popularity/combat cards. Ongoing bonus linked to section uncovered, triggered by self or immediate left/right taking that bottom action, not top/Factory. Announce actions. Active then left then right; sixth star immediately ends. In 2-player opponent triggers once.
grades.observed_answer: When enlisting, take a recruit from any bottom-row section and put it permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus on your Faction Mat. Immediately gain the selected one-time bonus: two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is determined by the circle uncovered where the recruit was removed, not by the one-time choice. For the rest of the game, when you or an immediate neighbor takes that corresponding bottom action, the bonus may trigger. Resolve active player first, then left neighbor, then right neighbor; stop if a sixth star ends the game. In two-player play, the opponent triggers it once, not twice.
grades.reader_evidence: Enlist: recruit goes to any open one-time space, bonus options, cannot later move; ongoing circle is where removed. Ongoing recruits: active, left, right sequence and two-player once rule.
grades.reason: Permanent open Faction placement, four one-time choices, uncovered-section ongoing trigger, active-left-right and two-player exception resolved.

grades.question: What may each combatant secretly spend on dial and cards, how do combat abilities resolve, and how are totals paid and ties broken?
grades.expected_answer: May fight at zero power/popularity. Attacker mech ability first, then defender. Dial 0 to min(current power,7). Up to one card per participating character/mech, even with zero dial. Reveal simultaneously; add card values, attacker wins tie. Both pay dial power and discard used cards face-up; card values do not reduce track.
grades.observed_answer: Both combatants simultaneously and secretly select dial power from zero to the smaller of seven and their current power. They may each add up to one combat card per participating character/mech, including with zero dial power; Rusviet People’s Army adds one additional card total if workers are present. If both players have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously, add dial power and card values, and the attacker wins ties. Both players pay their dial power from the power track and discard every played card face-up; card values do not cost track power.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat steps 1–3: ‘simultaneously and secretly’; dial limit; cards per participating character/mech; ability order; simultaneous reveal; attacker wins ties; both dial payments and card discard.
grades.reason: Capped dial/card spending, attacker-first abilities, simultaneous reveal/tie, both dial payments and used-card face-up discard resolved.

grades.question: After combat, what happens to all units/resources, popularity, combat stars, and the losing player combat-card reward?
grades.expected_answer: Winner controls territory/resources, places combat star if below two (Saxony unlimited available stars), may still fight after limit. Loser retreats all units including workers home leaving resources. Winning attacker loses one popularity per opposing worker retreated; winning defender does not. Loser draws one combat card if revealed at least one power on dial OR cards, none for zero total.
grades.observed_answer: The winner controls the territory and resources and places a combat star if eligible (normally up to two combat stars; Saxony may score without the usual limit within six available). Losing units—all characters, mechs, and workers—retreat to their home base, leaving all resources at the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy permits eligible units and carried workers to retreat to adjacent lakes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none. Polania Camaraderie has the stated combat exception. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat steps 4–5: winner controls and star; losing units retreat leaving resources; attacker popularity loss and defender exception; loser card draw condition.
grades.reason: Winner control/star limit, all-unit retreat/resources, attacker/defender popularity and dial-or-card loser reward resolved.

grades.question: When is an encounter resolved after contested entry, what if the character loses, where do gains go, and do normal action costs/bonuses apply?
grades.expected_answer: Character stops/cannot move again on entering token; finish Move and all combats before bottom action, only if character still there (must win contested entry). If loses token stays. Discard token, draw encounter, choose one affordable option (Polania up to two); pay printed cost and may decline benefits. Resources/structures/mechs/workers go to encounter territory. No additional normal costs/benefits or recruit bonuses; card face-down bottom encounter deck.
grades.observed_answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve an encounter if the character remains on the token territory. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the token stays. Discard the token and draw a card when resolving. Gains of resources, workers, mechs, or structures go to the encounter territory. Pay the printed encounter cost, but no normal action cost or Player Mat benefit applies, including no ongoing recruit bonuses.
grades.reader_evidence: Encounters: after Move and all combats; if contested entry is lost ‘the token stays’; gains go to encounter territory; ‘Pay no additional normal action costs’ and no mat/recruit benefits.
grades.reason: After-Move/all-combat encounter eligibility, losing-character token persistence, benefit destination and isolated costs/bonuses resolved.

grades.question: Who takes a Factory card, when, may later visitors take one or change theirs, and how do Factory actions and Speed movement differ from mat actions?
grades.expected_answer: Each character first finishing Move at Factory after any combat must choose one available card, return rest; not just first visitor, max one permanent card per player, cannot exchange. Fifth section, optional top then bottom; no corresponding mat coins/structure/recruit bonuses. Bottom Move one unit up to twice (three with character/mech Speed), same stop rules, Mine usable.
grades.observed_answer: Every player’s character must choose one available Factory card on that player’s first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning combat if necessary); this is not limited to the first visitor. Each player gets at most one permanent card and later visits cannot exchange it. A Factory card is a fifth action section with optional top then bottom and the usual no-repeat rule (Rusviet exception); its actions give no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories within that Move action, or three for a character/mech with Speed; Mine access and normal movement/stop rules apply.
grades.reader_evidence: Factory: ‘Every player’s character’ on first finish; at most one permanent card; fifth action section; no mat/recruit benefits; bottom Move distance and Speed.
grades.reason: Every character first-visit eligibility, after-Move choice, one permanent card, independent Factory bonuses and Speed/normal movement resolved.

grades.question: When can an objective be revealed, what requirements and discards apply, and what changes for Saxony?
grades.expected_answer: Only own turn before/after complete top or bottom action, all requirements true at reveal; may delay reveal. Place one objective star, discard both objectives to deck bottom. Saxony keeps second and may complete both, unrestricted combat/objective stars within six available.
grades.observed_answer: Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective. You must meet all requirements at the moment of reveal. Place the objective star and put both objective cards on the bottom of their deck. Normally only one objective star is allowed; Saxony retains the other card after the first and may score both.
grades.reader_evidence: Objectives and agreements: ‘Only on your own turn’; meet all requirements at reveal; place star and both cards on deck bottom; Saxony retains other card and can score both.
grades.reason: Own-turn complete-action timing, all requirements at reveal, deck-bottom discards and Saxony keep/score second resolved; specific card text was not requested.

grades.question: Which achievements earn stars, may stars be lost or another player block a goal, and when does the game end?
grades.expected_answer: Six upgrades, four mechs, four structures, four recruits, eight workers on board, completed objective, up to two combat victories, 18 popularity,16 power. Must place on achievement, each once except combat two/Saxony exception; irreversible and other players may share goals. Sixth star ends immediately, no extra turns/actions.
grades.observed_answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades; four deployed mechs; four built structures; four recruits; all eight workers on the board; one revealed completed objective; a combat victory (up to two stars, except Saxony); 18 popularity; or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony’s exception. Stars are permanent once placed even if power or popularity later falls, and other players’ stars do not block a goal. The sixth star immediately ends the game with no equalizing turns or further actions.
grades.reader_evidence: Stars and immediate end: full achievement list; goals awarded once; ‘A placed star is permanent’; other stars never block; sixth star immediately ends play.
grades.reason: All star achievements, permanence, shared goals and immediate sixth-star termination resolved.

grades.question: If a bottom action earns the sixth star, what is collected first; what happens to pending battles and a neighbor recruit star?
grades.expected_answer: Gain primary benefit, coins and own recruit ongoing benefit before placing bottom-action sixth star. Undo movement into any still-unresolved battle, return units to origin. Neighbor power/popularity star from recruit only after active action, in order active/left/right (clockwise), only if active did not already end game; stop remaining events at sixth star.
grades.observed_answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, collect its primary benefit, coins, and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing the star. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement by returning initiating units to their prior territories; do not resolve another combat. For neighbor power/popularity recruit stars, finish the active action, then resolve active player first, left neighbor, and right neighbor, checking for a sixth star at each step. If an earlier player places the sixth star, no later recruit star or bonus resolves.
grades.reader_evidence: Sixth-star sequence: ‘primary benefit, coins and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing’; pending battle movement undone; active, left, right sequence and stop rule.
grades.reason: Pre-star bottom benefits, pending-battle rollback and neighbor recruit priority/interruption resolved.

grades.question: At 10 popularity, how much do 5 stars, 4 normal territories plus Factory, and 13 resources add to held coins? Include structure bonus eligibility and all victory tiebreakers.
grades.expected_answer: Tier 7-12 pays $4/star,$3/territory,$2/resource pair. 5 stars=$20; 4+Factory as 3=7 territories=$21; six pairs=$12, total $53 plus held coins and structure tile. Structure bonus even without control. Most coins wins; ties workers+mechs+structures (not character), power, popularity, controlled resources, controlled territories, placed stars.
grades.observed_answer: At 10 popularity, the 7–12 tier pays $4 per star, $3 per controlled territory, and $2 per complete pair of controlled resources. Five stars add $20; four normal territories plus Factory count as seven territories and add $21; 13 resources make six complete pairs and add $12, total $53 in addition to held coins. The selected structure bonus is also scored, even if enemies control your structure territories. Tiebreakers, in order: workers + mechs + structures (not character), power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, stars placed.
grades.reader_evidence: Final fortune table and example: ‘$20 + $21 + $12 = $53’; structure bonus even if enemies control; tie-break order.
grades.reason: Tier-2 rates, Factory as three, floor pairs and $53, retained coins/structure eligibility and exact tiebreak order resolved.

grades.question: Is a home base a territory, may you enter one normally, and are expansion home bases active?
grades.expected_answer: Home base is not territory for any game effect; cannot normally move back in, build/deploy there. Starts and forced retreat exceptions; Crimea Wayfare explicit movement exception. Two unrepresented bases are expansion placeholders/inactive.
grades.observed_answer: A home base is not a territory for any game effect. Normally you cannot move into any home base, build there, or deploy there; setup and forced retreats are exceptions, as is Crimea’s unlocked Wayfare. Two bases without matching core factions are inactive expansion placeholders.
grades.reader_evidence: Control, resources and home bases: ‘A home base is not a territory’; default restrictions and exceptions; inactive expansion placeholders.
grades.reason: Non-territory home base/default prohibitions, explicit exceptions and inactive expansion placeholders resolved.

grades.question: Which terrain produces each token, do Factory/lake produce, are workers resources, and what happens if resource supply runs out?
grades.expected_answer: Mountain metal; tundra oil; farm food; forest wood; village workers. Lake/Factory nothing. Workers not resources. Resource supply unlimited; use multipliers as necessary, no territory token/unit limit.
grades.observed_answer: Mountain produces metal, tundra oil, farm food, forest wood, and village a worker. Lake and Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.
grades.reader_evidence: Produce terrain table; resources definition says workers are not resources; ‘Resource tokens have no supply limit: use multipliers if needed.’
grades.reason: All terrain outputs/no-output spaces, nonresource workers, unlimited resources and territory quantities resolved.

grades.question: May resources be picked up/dropped mid-movement, can mechs carry characters, and what does unlocked Speed change about tunnels and stops?
grades.expected_answer: All units may pick/drop any resources; mechs also own workers, never character. Speed adds one territory for character/mechs, including before/after tunnel jump which costs one move; may pick/drop mid-move. Entering enemy unit ends movement/cannot move again turn; character encounter also stops.
grades.observed_answer: All units can pick up, carry, and drop any number of resources during movement; a mech may also carry any number of your workers, but never your character. A carried worker may move itself later in the turn. Speed adds one territory of movement to each selected character/mech, not workers. A tunnel jump costs one movement step, with the extra Speed step usable before or after it. A mech can pick up/drop resources and workers mid-movement. Enemy-unit stops and character encounter stops override Speed.
grades.reader_evidence: Move: unit carrying rules; Speed: adds one territory, tunnel jump costs one step, extra step before/after; stops override Speed.
grades.reason: All-unit resource pickup/drop, mech own-worker/no-character carriage, Speed/tunnel step and overriding stops resolved.

grades.question: Can workers capture a territory controlled only by an enemy structure, and are printed tunnels usable by all unit types?
grades.expected_answer: Yes any unit may enter structure-only territory and controls it; no combat from structure alone. All printed tunnel territories adjacent for Move by any unit; enemy Mine not a public tunnel.
grades.observed_answer: Yes. Any unit may enter a territory held only by an enemy structure, taking control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit type.
grades.reader_evidence: Move: ‘All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit’; ‘Any unit may enter a territory held only by an enemy structure.’
grades.reason: Any unit captures enemy structure-only territory, no structure combat, all-unit printed tunnels versus personal Mine resolved.

grades.question: If unable to afford any action after last using Move, must you pay a partial Produce cost or what turn is legal?
grades.expected_answer: Never partial payment; full cost required. Take a dead turn choosing another section with no actions, still moving token.
grades.observed_answer: You do not have to pay a partial Produce cost. If unable to afford any action, move your token to a different section and take neither action; this is a legal dead turn. You must move the token, and never pay only part of a cost.
grades.reader_evidence: Turn Structure: ‘If unable to afford any action, take a dead turn’; ‘Never pay only part of a cost.’
grades.reason: Full payment required; legal dead turn shifts token and takes neither action resolved.

grades.question: What do Armory and Monument grant, when do those benefits trigger, and can an enemy occupant take them away?
grades.expected_answer: Armory adds 1 power when owner takes Trade, Monument adds 1 popularity when owner takes Bolster. Uncovered benefits apply future respective top actions, regardless territory control; opponent never gains them. Factory similar actions excluded.
grades.observed_answer: A built Armory grants one power when you take Trade; a built Monument grants one popularity when you take Bolster. These are matching top-action bonuses. You keep a building’s abilities even without controlling its territory, and enemy units do not gain them, so an enemy occupant does not take them away.
grades.reader_evidence: Bolster/Trade building bonuses; control section: ‘You keep those abilities even without control’; enemies do not gain them.
grades.reason: Trade Armory power/Bolster Monument popularity, future triggering and owner persistence versus enemy control resolved.

grades.question: How does each base faction Riverwalk differ, which units receive it, and does Nordic Swim give lake movement or help its mechs?
grades.expected_answer: Riverwalk only character/mechs: Saxony and Nordic forests/mountains; Rusviet farms/villages; Crimea farms/tundra; Polania villages/mountains. Nordic faction Swim workers only across rivers to any land terrain, never lakes; no mech/character benefit.
grades.observed_answer: Riverwalk is for the character and mechs: Rusviet can enter farms and villages; Crimea farms and tundra; Nordic forests and mountains; Polania villages and mountains; Saxony forests and mountains. Nordic Swim is the starting special ability for workers alone: they may cross rivers to any land terrain, not lakes. It does not help Nordic character/mechs.
grades.reader_evidence: Faction/Riverwalk table; Nordic Swim: workers alone cross rivers to land terrain, not lakes; does not help character/mechs.
grades.reason: All five Riverwalk terrain pairs/character-mech scope and worker-only Nordic river/not-lake Swim resolved.

grades.question: Which locations become adjacent under Saxony Underpass and Rusviet Township, and which units can use those shortcuts?
grades.expected_answer: Underpass controlled mountains and all tunnels (including own Mine) adjacent for character/mechs. Township controlled villages and Factory adjacent for character/mechs. Not workers; required ability unlocked via deploy.
grades.observed_answer: Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels, including its Mine, adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions. These shortcuts are for characters and mechs, not workers.
grades.reader_evidence: Other unlocked mech abilities: Underpass and Township descriptions both specify character/mech Move actions.
grades.reason: Saxony controlled mountains+tunnels and Rusviet controlled villages+Factory, character/mech-only adjacency resolved.

grades.question: When does Saxony Disarm apply, how often, and how does Nordic Artillery differ?
grades.expected_answer: Disarm before combat on printed tunnel or own Mine: opponent loses 2 power once per combat, not per unit. Artillery before any combat may pay 1 power to make opponent lose 2, once per combat. Track losses; attacker ability before defender.
grades.observed_answer: Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or Saxony’s Mine: the opponent loses two power on the track, once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery may be used before combat by paying one power to reduce the opponent’s power by two, once per combat, not per unit.

Pay all exposed red-box costs in full before taking as much or as little of the exposed green-box benefit as desired; exact bottom costs and coin benefits vary by Player Mat and upgrades.

Exposing new costs affects future Produce actions, not the cost already paid.

grades.reason: Full exposed pre-payment, terrain production, left-to-right village workers, optional benefits and future-cost timing resolved.

grades.question: What may each combatant secretly spend on dial and cards, how do combat abilities resolve, and how are totals paid and ties broken?

If both have combat mech abilities, attacker uses theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously and add dial and card values; attacker wins ties. grades.reader_evidence: Combat steps 1–3 specify simultaneous secret choices, card limits, ability order, reveal, payment, and attacker tie-break.
grades.reason: Capped dial/card spending, attacker-first abilities, simultaneous reveal/tie, both dial payments and used-card face-up discard resolved.

All losing characters, mechs, and workers retreat to their home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy allows eligible units/carried workers to retreat to adjacent lakes instead. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none. Loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser gets none.
grades.reader_evidence: Combat step 4–5 covers retreats, resources, attacker popularity, stars, and loser's card draw.
grades.reason: Winner control/star limit, all-unit retreat/resources, attacker/defender popularity and dial-or-card loser reward resolved.

Pay the printed option cost, but no normal action cost or mat benefits apply, including no ongoing recruit bonuses.

For neighbor recruit power/popularity stars: finish the active action, then resolve active player, left neighbor, right neighbor, checking for a sixth star each time; if an earlier player places the sixth star, no later recruit star or bonus resolves.

grades.reader_evidence: Camaraderie description explicitly limits it to combat and excludes undefended-worker removal.
grades.reason: Camaraderie only combat-winning aggressor/on-own-turn; no undefended-worker displacement exception resolved.

grades.question: How does Polania Meander resolve encounters, including card count, options and paying the second option?
grades.expected_answer: Draw just one card; may choose up to two different options in either order; may use first benefit to pay second cost.
grades.observed_answer: Meander allows Polania to choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order. The first option's gain may pay the second option's cost. The summary does not state a separate procedural rule specifically requiring a second-option payment beyond the general rule that printed costs must be paid; any unaffordable option cannot be selected.
grades.reader_evidence: Polania Meander: up to two different options in either order; first gain can pay second cost. Encounter options require printed cost and unaffordable coin/popularity options cannot be selected.
grades.reason: One card/up to two different options, either order and first gain paying second resolved.

grades.question: If a character reaches an encounter during Factory bottom Move, can it continue moving, and does the encounter occur before all combats finish?
grades.expected_answer: No character movement again that turn; Factory Move obeys stop rules. Encounter after entire Move and all combats; character must remain there. Bottom Factory Move still triggers normal encounter.
grades.observed_answer: No. A character entering an encounter territory stops and cannot move again that turn, including during Factory Move. The encounter resolves after the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there.
grades.reader_evidence: Move encounter stop rule; Encounters section timing also applies during Factory Move.
grades.reason: Factory Move encounter stop and after-all-combats timing resolved.

grades.question: What information about coins, combat cards and objectives is public, and is the exact coin total required on request?

grades.observed_answer: Combat-card count is public but contents are secret; objective contents are secret. Coins are not hidden information, but the summary says a player need not reveal their total coin value. During combat players may conceal whether they committed cards until reveal.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup information section.
grades.reason: Coin information/optional total disclosure, combat count versus contents/commitment concealment and objective secrecy resolved.

grades.question: Which things can be exchanged in alliances, are agreements enforceable, and can a payment cancel combat once begun?
grades.expected_answer: Only tangible exchange coins (tournament exception no coin trades for deals/alliances); informal agreements unenforceable. Cannot cancel already initiated combat by negotiation; must fight after Move, though bribes may influence outcome.

A payment cannot cancel combat once initiated by moving units onto opposing units; the fight occurs after Move, though bribes may influence its outcome.
grades.reader_evidence: Objectives and agreements section.
grades.reason: Only coin exchanges/tournament exception, unenforceable agreements and mandatory initiated combat resolved.

grades.question: State all final-scoring popularity tiers and payouts; do controlled lakes and home bases count, and do leftover single resources score?
grades.expected_answer: 0-6: stars3/territories2/pairs1;7-12:4/3/2;13-18:5/4/3. Lakes count if controlled, home bases never. Factory three total. Sum controlled resources across board and score floor(total/2), no leftover single; workers not resources.
grades.observed_answer: At popularity 0–6, each star scores $3, territory $2, and resource pair $1; at 7–12, $4, $3, and $2; at 13–18, $5, $4, and $3. Controlled lakes count; home bases do not. Pool controlled resources and score complete pairs only, ignoring an odd leftover.
grades.reader_evidence: Final fortune table and scoring explanation.
grades.reason: All three scoring tiers/rates, lakes/home/Factory, pooled floor pairs/no workers resolved.

grades.question: For adjacent-tunnel, adjacent-encounter and adjacent-lake structure bonuses, how are duplicates, rivers, removed encounters and Mines treated, and what are the payouts?
grades.expected_answer: Count each qualifying adjacent feature once across structures. Rivers do not break adjacency; removed encounter tokens still count printed encounter. Mine not tunnel for tile. Adjacent tunnels count1=$2,2-3=$4,4-5=$6,6=$9; lakes/encounters1=$2,2-3=$4,4-5=$6,6-7=$9; zero=$0.
grades.observed_answer: For each selected adjacency tile, count each unique qualifying feature once across all your structures. Tunnels are unique printed tunnels, not Mines; lakes are unique lakes; encounter locations are unique printed locations even if the token has been removed. Rivers do not break adjacency. Payouts for each of the three tiles (tunnels, lakes, encounters) are: 1 feature $2; 2–3 $4; 4–5 $6; 6 (or 6–7 for lakes/encounters) $9. Zero scores zero.
grades.reader_evidence: Structure bonus table and notes: unique features, printed tunnels not Mines, removed encounter tokens count, rivers do not break adjacency.
grades.reason: Three adjacency tile features/unique counting/rivers/removed encounter/Mine exception and exact payout ranges resolved.

grades.question: For structures on tunnels, structures in a row, and structures on farms/tundras, what qualifies and what are the payouts?
grades.expected_answer: On printed tunnels not Mine:1=$2,2=$4,3-4=$6. Longest continuous straight line only, rivers do not break:1=$2,2=$4,3=$6,4=$9. Farms+tundras combined number with structures:1=$2,2=$4,3=$6,4=$9. Zero=$0. Bonus regardless territory control.
grades.observed_answer: Structures on tunnels count structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1 $2, 2 $4, 3–4 $6. Structures in a row score only your longest continuous straight line: 1 $2, 2 $4, 3 $6, 4 $9. Structures on farms/tundras count qualifying structures combined: 1 $2, 2 $4, 3 $6, 4 $9. Rivers do not break a straight row.
grades.reader_evidence: Structure bonus table and note that rivers do not break a straight row.
grades.reason: Printed-tunnel versus Mine, longest continuous straight row/rivers, combined farm+tundra and each exact payout resolved.

grades.question: In combat on a lake, does a winning attacker lose popularity for workers carried by the defeated mech?
grades.expected_answer: Yes one popularity per forced-retreat worker even carried on lake; retreat with mech to home base by default (Nordic Seaworthy permits adjacent-lake retreat). Polania unlocked Camaraderie exception after combat.

grades.reader_evidence: Combat step 5 explicitly includes workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.
grades.reason: Winning lake attacker loses popularity for carried defeated workers, normal retreat and named faction exceptions resolved.

grades.question: Does placing a popularity star protect current popularity or its scoring tier, and can two factions both star the same achievement?
grades.expected_answer: Star itself permanent, popularity may fall and final payout uses current tier. Other factions may also place same goal; no blocking.
grades.observed_answer: No. A popularity star is permanent, but current popularity determines final scoring, so it does not protect the current amount or tier. Other players' stars never block a goal, so two factions can each earn a star for the same achievement.
grades.reader_evidence: Stars section says star remains if popularity drops and other players' stars never block a goal; current popularity determines scoring.
grades.reason: Permanent star versus mutable current scoring tier, other factions sharing goal resolved.

grades.question: How are Faction Mats and Player Mats assigned, and in what relative faction order should players sit? Why does that seating matter for recruit bonuses?
grades.expected_answer: Randomly shuffle the Faction Mats and Player Mats and deal one of each to each player. source_references: Rulebook PDF p. 20: ONGOING BONUS and PLAYER ORDER
grades.observed_answer: Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions in board order: Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania clockwise, omitting inactive factions. Seating determines who counts as your immediate left/right neighbor for ongoing recruit bonuses triggered by bottom-row actions.
grades.reader_evidence: Setup mat assignment/seating and Ongoing recruits neighbor rule.

grades.question: For movement, what distinguishes a river from a lake, and from which surrounding land territories can a unit with a lake-movement ability enter the lake?
grades.expected_answer: A river lies on the border between two land territories. A lake comprises an entire territory hex and extends from that hex to any adjacent shoreline. A unit with the appropriate lake-movement ability can move onto it from any of the surrounding territories shown by that shoreline; crossing permission for a river alone does not grant entry to lakes.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p. 11: RIVERS AND LAKES; RIVER; LAKE; illustrated example
grades.observed_answer: Rivers are borders between land hexes; lakes are entire territories adjoining surrounding shores. Normally units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes. The summary says unlocked lake abilities permit character/mechs to move to/from lakes, but does not specify which surrounding land hexes qualify as entry points; that detail is unsupported by the summary.
grades.reader_evidence: Control section defines rivers and lakes; lake abilities state character/mechs move to/from lakes without specifying qualifying shore hexes.
grades.reason: The river-versus-lake distinction is correct, but the answer expressly leaves which surrounding land hexes permit lake entry unsupported. The source resolves this as all surrounding shoreline-adjacent territories. Independently adjudicated in expanded01-adjudication.json.

grades.question: Must the next player wait until the current player has finished every bottom-row decision, or when may the next turn begin?
grades.expected_answer: The next clockwise player may begin when the current player starts or is finalizing a bottom-row action, while the current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure or recruit to gain. source_references: Rulebook PDF p10 GAMEPLAY, paragraph beginning After you have completed your turn

grades.reason: Next clockwise player may begin while noninteractive bottom-action decision is underway; priority/end restrictions retained.

grades.question: After taking the selected top-row or bottom-row action, may you pay its cost again to take that same action a second time in the same turn?

grades.question: After you achieve a star goal, may you decline or delay placing that star to avoid ending the game? How does this differ from holding a completed objective card unrevealed?

grades.reader_evidence: Stars: place as soon as achieved, sixth ends immediately. Objectives: may wait to reveal completed objective.
grades.reason: Earned threshold star placement mandatory/immediate; completed objective reveal may wait while requirements hold resolved.

grades.question: While you control the territory containing your Mill, how does it affect the number of territories you may Produce on and the output there, including when no actual worker is present?
grades.expected_answer: The Mill territory may count as an extra bonus territory in addition to the normal territories selected for Produce. The Mill produces as if it were one worker, so it can produce even with no actual worker there. Any actual workers on its territory may also produce.

It never says that actual workers on the Mill territory also produce, leaving the requested output there incomplete. Three total describes the ordinary default count in context; it is not treated as an express cap after upgrades. Independently adjudicated in expanded01-adjudication.json.

grades.question: What presence establishes control of a territory, and do resources alone preserve your control after your last unit leaves a territory where you have no structure?
grades.expected_answer: You control a territory with at least one of your units, or with your structure and no enemy units. Resources are not units and do not establish control. If your last unit leaves and you have no structure there, you no longer control that territory or the resources left there; those resources cannot be spent by you unless you regain control.
source_references: Rulebook PDF p4, CONTROL: control requires at least one unit or a structure with no enemy units; only one player controls a territory at a time.
Rulebook PDF p4, RESOURCES: resource tokens remain on the board and may be spent only from territories currently controlled.
Rulebook PDF p29, EVERY TERRITORY CONTROLLED and EVERY 2 RESOURCES CONTROLLED; PDF p31, END-GAME SCORING.
grades.observed_answer: A territory is controlled if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not establish control; if your last unit leaves and you have no structure, resources there do not preserve your control. An enemy worker alone on your structure territory controls it and its resources.
grades.reader_evidence: Control definition; resources are not listed as establishing control.
grades.reason: Control needs unit or own structure without enemy units; resources alone do not maintain control/spending after last unit leaves resolved.
